content: Endothall is a chemical compound utilized as an herbicide for managing both terrestrial and aquatic plants. Specifically, it is employed as an aquatic herbicide to control submerged aquatic vegetation and algae in bodies of water such as lakes, ponds, and irrigation canals. Additionally, it is used as a desiccant for crops like potatoes, hops, cotton, clover, and alfalfa. Endothall also functions as a biocide to regulate the growth of mollusks and algae in industrial cooling towers. Its chemical formula is C8H10O5, and its Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) name is 7-oxabicycloheptane-2,3-dicarboxylic acid. Although it is an organic acid, it is typically applied in the form of its dipotassium salt or mono-N,N-dimethylalkylamine salt. Exposure to water contaminated with endothall at levels exceeding the maximum contaminant level (MCL) established by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) over prolonged periods may lead to gastrointestinal issues, including stomach or intestinal problems, in some individuals.
